title: DPRK supply chain campaign against logistics software

sections.heading: Executive Summary
sections.body: A DPRK-attributed cluster is compromising logistics software vendors to reach downstream operators. One UAE logistics operator is a confirmed downstream consumer of the trojanised update channel. CPX assesses follow-on intrusion attempts within the next two weeks as likely.

sections.heading: TIC Analysis
sections.body: Overlaps with tracked Lazarus subgroup tooling: matching loader export hashes, shared C2 certificate issuer, and a packing routine seen in two prior campaigns. Victimology is consistent with revenue generation rather than espionage. Source: CrowdStrike Falcon X, Actors.

sections.heading: Campaign Overview
sections.body: The campaign trojanises a fleet management suite's update package. Installations fetch the package over plain HTTP, and the actor substitutes a signed but stale certificate. Three vendors are confirmed affected; one supplies two GCC logistics groups.

sections.heading: Attack Chain Overview
sections.body: Initial access through the poisoned update, a staged loader with a five day sleep, then credential theft from the fleet telemetry database and lateral movement over RDP toward finance systems.

sections.body: Techniques observed in this campaign are mapped in the table below.

sections.heading: Recommendations
sections.body: Block the listed infrastructure, verify the integrity of fleet management software updates against vendor checksums, and hunt for the loader's scheduled task names across the estate.

title: wp2shell follow-on: two further WordPress theme flaws

sections.heading: Executive Summary
sections.body: Two further vulnerabilities in the theme framework abused by the wp2shell campaign are now public. One is exploited in the wild; the second has proof-of-concept code circulating. Prose in this advisory follows the WPScan severity ordering.

sections.heading: Impact
sections.body: Successful exploitation yields unauthenticated remote code execution in the web server context on the higher ranked flaw, and authenticated arbitrary file read on the second.

sections.heading: CVSS v3 Base Score
sections.body: Scores and their authorities are recorded in the score table. The two authorities rank these CVEs in the opposite order.

sections.heading: Affected Products and Versions
sections.body: Theme framework versions 4.2.0 through 4.6.1 across all bundled themes. Version 4.6.2 fixes both flaws.

sections.heading: Existence of Public Exploit
sections.body: Public exploit code exists for CVE-2026-31042. Proof-of-concept only for CVE-2026-31055.

sections.heading: Exploit Status
sections.body: CVE-2026-31042 is exploited in the wild against unpatched sites. No in-the-wild exploitation observed for CVE-2026-31055.

sections.heading: TTPs Mapping
sections.body: Techniques observed in exploitation of these flaws are mapped in the table below.

sections.heading: Detection and Hunting
sections.body: Hunt for POST requests to theme preview endpoints followed by PHP file writes under wp-content/uploads. Detection logic for the loader is referenced in the campaign advisory.

sections.heading: Mitigation and Recommendation
sections.body: Update the theme framework to 4.6.2, restrict write access to wp-content, and review upload directories for recently created PHP files.
